nodes.body: The raised `RateLimitError` drops the original diagnostic that triggered detection (stderr / JSON `message`), which makes the “UNDETERMINED” summary and action log less actionable when debugging. Consider including a safely-truncated matched snippet (e.g., first N chars, single-line) inside `RateLimitError` (or as an attribute) so `_rate_limit_verdict` can report what was actually observed without making any further API calls.

The fixed diagnostic is deliberate. A matched API diagnostic can include caller details (for example, the client address in a primary-limit message), and truncation alone does not sanitize that content. This path reports the actionable outcome—an explicit rate-limit refusal, a nonzero UNDETERMINED verdict, and no further requests—without echoing API text. Actual independent Opus review considered and accepted this trade-off on the current head 54dd9e912195658b89658394a3ee31a68c208a77. Keeping the safe constant here; structured diagnostic categories could be added separately if operational evidence warrants them.

`_rate_limit_verdict` interpolates `({exc})`, but `RateLimitError` currently always uses a fixed message, so this parenthetical doesn’t add information and increases noise in the summary. Either remove the `({exc})` portion or (preferably) populate `RateLimitError` with the sanitized triggering diagnostic so the message becomes genuinely informative.

Agreed that the parenthetical currently adds little information. I am retaining the generic exception detail as a nonblocking presentation nit in this fix. The deliberate boundary is that API response text is not copied into the job summary; the surrounding message already identifies the refusal and says that polling/recovery stopped. This is the same diagnostic trade-off considered and accepted in the independent Opus review of 54dd9e912195658b89658394a3ee31a68c208a77; no passing result or hidden retry depends on the wording.
